title: Promising
body: I have really enjoyed this merge game, but have a bit of feedback: Most of the merge games I’ve played all refill your energy/gives you a set amount when you level up. This one doesn’t, and it’s a bit maddening … I don’t mind paying for occasional packs or event perks, but I’m probably going to stop playing this one soon as I’m level 22 and just blow through energy way too fast compared to getting energy items or via quests. It’s not fun when you have to buy multiple add-ons a day just to keep playing. Also, it would be SO great if you were able to zoom in/out of the background, or could delay a decor choice instead of being forced into it with a limited visual range. It makes it hard to decide how an option looks among other choices in the space. That’s been a frustration with most decor choices. I’d also love a less … froofy set of decor options? I don’t really love the froofy stuff, or most of the green or orange stuff. And I really don’t like all the angel statues that you have no choice about adding to your space. That said, I find the story proceeds at a better pace than other popular merge games. Or you are at least given enough info to come to some conclusions and maintain interest. Overall it’s solid, but I hope some energy gifts or level refills are incorporated soon. The minor gripes are easier to overlook if you can just keep playing longer. Oh, and I’d kill for an alternative or “goth” set of options! Ella is an alternative lady, she should have a bit more decor to match the vibe. 😉

title: Best story I've seen in a merge game
body: I've dabbled in a lot of merge games and usually bounce off them because the writing is so irritating. So many of these games abandon their plot premises or pad for time by making characters almost pathologically non-confrontational. I knew Just Desserts would be special when the protagonist learned key information about a suspect and *immediately* called to question them about it. Even when dessert business events take focus, the plot and characters of Just Desserts never forget that their main concern is the mystery of the fire. Rather than drag things out, characters act on information quickly, and setbacks emerge in the form of new twists or even actual physical threats from the antagonists. A cozy mobile game mystery with real tension! Amazing!!! The writers have even made the ex both remorseful and helpful enough to be a viable contender as a love interest. Unlike in other games, it's easy to understand why Ella keeps getting pulled back into his orbit, even if you're rooting for her to get with someone else (PS please give me more time with my boy Hank thank you). I haven't felt this way about a mobile game's writing since Stella Sacco wrote for Lily's Garden. It's such a breath of fresh air in this space, and I sincerely hope this company appreciates their writers as much as I do.
